deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Governs Terraform's lifecycle behaviour on destroy (DELETE/PREVENT/ABANDON). This is an operational/state-management control rather than a cloud security control; it does not change how the gateway peers or which endpoints it connects to.

description.description: An optional description of this resource.
description.rationale: A free-text description for human reference. It has no effect on the resource's security configuration.

labels.description:
Labels for the external VPN gateway resource.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Key/value metadata for organisation, billing, and filtering. Labels do not enforce access or connectivity controls; they are informational and non-authoritative, so they carry no direct security impact.

name.description:
Name of the resource. Provided by the client when the resource is
created. The name must be 1-63 characters long, and comply with
RFC1035.  Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters long and
match the regular expression '[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?' which means
the first character must be a lowercase letter, and all following
characters must be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit, except the last
character, which cannot be a dash.
name.rationale: The resource identifier. Naming conventions may aid governance, but the name itself does not affect confidentiality, integrity, or the connectivity established by the gateway.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Specifies the owning project. Project placement affects organisation and IAM boundaries at a higher level, but as a gateway argument it selects an existing project rather than configuring any security control on the resource, so it is treated as non-security-relevant.

redundancy_type.description: Indicates the redundancy type of this external VPN gateway Possible values: ["FOUR_IPS_REDUNDANCY", "SINGLE_IP_INTERNALLY_REDUNDANT", "TWO_IPS_REDUNDANCY"]
redundancy_type.rationale: Selects the high-availability topology (number of redundant interfaces) for the gateway. This is an availability/resilience choice; it affects tunnel uptime rather than the confidentiality or access controls of the connection, so it is treated as non-security-relevant. (Availability requirements, where they exist, are typically enforced at the HA-VPN design level rather than as a policy on this argument.)

interface.description: A list of interfaces on this external VPN gateway.

interface.id.description:
The numeric ID for this interface. Allowed values are based on the redundancy type
of this external VPN gateway
* '0 - SINGLE_IP_INTERNALLY_REDUNDANT'
* '0, 1 - TWO_IPS_REDUNDANCY'
* '0, 1, 2, 3 - FOUR_IPS_REDUNDANCY'
interface.id.rationale: An index that maps an interface to a slot determined by the redundancy type. It is a structural identifier within the gateway definition and does not itself configure a security control, so it is non-security-relevant.

interface.ip_address.description:
IP address of the interface in the external VPN gateway.
Only IPv4 is supported. This IP address can be either from
your on-premise gateway or another Cloud provider's VPN gateway,
it cannot be an IP address from Google Compute Engine.
interface.ip_address.rationale: Specifies the external (on-prem or other-cloud) IPv4 peer endpoint that this gateway will establish VPN tunnels with. This value defines the remote trust boundary — the specific external peer allowed to terminate an encrypted tunnel into the environment. Policy should restrict peer IP addresses to an approved allowlist and reject broad, unspecified, or unexpected ranges, since an incorrect or untrusted peer endpoint directly determines who can connect the VPN.

interface.ipv6_address.description:
IPv6 address of the interface in the external VPN gateway. This IPv6
address can be either from your on-premise gateway or another Cloud
provider's VPN gateway, it cannot be an IP address from Google Compute
Engine. Must specify an IPv6 address (not IPV4-mapped) using any format
described in RFC 4291 (e.g. 2001:db8:0:0:2d9:51:0:0). The output format
is RFC 5952 format (e.g. 2001:db8::2d9:51:0:0).
interface.ipv6_address.rationale: Specifies the external IPv6 peer endpoint that this gateway will establish VPN tunnels with. Like the IPv4 interface address, it defines the remote trust boundary — the external peer permitted to terminate an encrypted tunnel. Policy should restrict peer IPv6 addresses to an approved allowlist and ensure IPv6 peers are subject to the same review and firewall controls as IPv4 peers.

params.description: Additional params passed with the request, but not persisted as part of resource payload

params.resource_manager_tags.description:
Resource manager tags to be bound to the ExternalVpnGateway. Tag keys and values have the
same definition as resource manager tags. Keys must be in the format tagKeys/{tag_key_id},
and values are in the format tagValues/456.
params.resource_manager_tags.rationale: Binds Resource Manager tags to the external VPN gateway. Tags can drive IAM conditions and organisation-policy enforcement, so they participate directly in access-control decisions. Policy can require governance-mandated tags (e.g. data-classification or environment) to be present where the organisation uses tag-based conditional access.
